name: Tofacitinib Citrate
meta: Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor – targeted synthetic DMARD
sections: 312.38 g/mol (base); 504.49 g/mol (citrate; 8 mg citrate ≈ 5 mg base)
Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor – targeted synthetic DMARD
White to off-white powder (citrate), slightly soluble in water.

Approved for RA (2012), ulcerative colitis (2018), polyarticular JIA (2020) and ankylosing spondylitis (2021). The ORAL Surveillance trial (2021) showed higher MACE, malignancy and thrombosis versus TNF inhibitors in patients ≥50 with CV risk factors, prompting boxed warnings. First approval/introduction: US FDA November 2012 (Pfizer).

Inhibits JAK1 and JAK3 (and to lesser extent JAK2), blocking STAT signalling of cytokines (IL-2, IL-6, IL-7, IL-15, IL-21, interferons) and reducing immune-mediated inflammation. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits JAK1 and JAK3 (and to a lesser degree JAK2), interrupting JAK–STAT signalling of multiple pro-inflammatory cytokines.
Summary: Bioavailability ~74%; Tmax 0.5–1 h. ~40% protein bound. ~70% hepatic (CYP3A4, minor 2C19); ~30% renal. Half-life ~3 h.
Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis (with methotrexate or alone) after inadequate response to DMARDs
Moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (specialist use)
RA / PsA / AS: 5 mg twice daily
UC: 10 mg twice daily for 8 weeks (induction), then 5 mg twice daily
Moderate–severe renal or moderate hepatic impairment: 5 mg once daily
Interrupt for serious infection or if lymphocytes <500, ANC <1000, Hb <8 g/dL
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Moderate: 5 mg once daily; severe: avoid.
Higher risk of infection, MACE, malignancy – use only if no alternative in ≥65 years.
Contraindicated; use effective contraception during and 4 weeks after therapy.
Active serious infections including active TB
Absolute neutrophil count <1000/mm³, lymphocytes <500/mm³ or Hb <8 g/dL (do not start)
Serious infections, TB reactivation, herpes zoster – screen for latent TB and hepatitis B/C before starting
Major adverse cardiovascular events and malignancy – especially age ≥65, smokers, CV risk factors
Monitor lymphocytes, neutrophils, Hb, lipids, LFTs
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole) or moderate CYP3A4 + strong CYP2C19 inhibitors (fluconazole) – reduce to 5 mg once daily
With or without food; avoid grapefruit.
Lymphocytes, neutrophils, Hb at baseline, 4–8 weeks, then every 3 months; lipids at 4–8 weeks; LFTs; latent TB and hepatitis screening; skin cancer checks.
Supportive care; monitor for infection and cytopenias.
OCTAVE (Sandborn et al., NEJM 2017) – effective induction and maintenance in ulcerative colitis.
ORAL Surveillance (Ytterberg et al., NEJM 2022) – higher MACE and cancer than TNF inhibitors in at-risk RA patients.
Report fever, cough, burning urination, shingles rash
Report leg swelling, chest pain, breathlessness
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
